newsitem.title: UK: BBA makes Italy buy, seals China venture.
newsitem.headline: BBA makes Italy buy, seals China venture.

text.p: British-based engineering and materials firm BBA Group Plc said on Tuesday it had agreed to buy privately-owned Italian materials company Korma for between 4.0 and 12 million stg, subject to performance.
In the same statement, the company said it had signed a framework agreement for a joint venture to produce friction materials near Beijing, in China.

"BBA will be the majority partner in a green field development...to be operational in 1998. The initial business objective of the new venture will be to support existing European customers already building vehicles in China," it said.
Korma specialises in the development and manufacture of super absorbent materials for the global hygiene market which had sales of 11 million stg last year.
"These are two important moves for BBA," chief executive Roberto Quarta said, adding that the technology used by Korma should provide "exciting opportunities for growth".
The China joint venture would give the company what he called an important position in the expanding market.
Earlier on Tuesday BBA reported pre-tax profits of 141.1 million stg for calendar 1996, at the lower end of a range of market expectations.
The dividend payment of 7.0 pence, while up on last year's 6.0 pence, was also less than market expectations of between 7.1 and 7.3 pence.
After the results were announced, BBA's shares eased to stand down 6-1/2 pence at 361-1/2 pence by 0920 GMT.
In his comments on the results, Quarta highlighted the increased after-market content in group business which he said was one factor positioning the group for continued growth.
